findings.rationale: CT's local performance is far off: AUC 0.599 (z=-6.7), ECE 0.153 (z=+14.1), CITL -0.152 (z=-11.2), observed prevalence 0.281 versus mean predicted 0.129. Low AUC together with inflated prevalence is the signature of flipped outcome labels, not a prevalence shift (which would keep AUC normal). The O/E ratio is elevated across both sex subgroups (about 2.4 and 1.9), consistent with uniform label flipping rather than subgroup-specific under-diagnosis. Its updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 4.6, mean cos -0.72, z around -9), which fits training on wrong labels. The per-round drift table shows CITL negative from round 2 onward and prevalence around 0.22-0.37 throughout, so the fault looks present from the start.

UT's local AUC is 0.615 (z=-6.2), ECE 0.165 (z=+16.0), CITL -0.160 (z=-11.9), and observed prevalence 0.278 against mean predicted 0.118. This again matches flipped labels: AUC is depressed while prevalence is inflated. The O/E ratio is high in every sex and income subgroup (about 2.6 and 2.2 for sex, 2.5 for income group 5), so the bias is uniform rather than concentrated in one subgroup. Its updates are the largest in the federation (median norm ratio 5.9, mean cos -0.73, z around -9), consistent with training on corrupted labels. CITL is already negative at round 1 (-0.099) and stays negative through round 20.

VT's local AUC is 0.574 (z=-7.3), ECE 0.122 (z=+10.4), CITL -0.119 (z=-8.8), and observed prevalence 0.242 against mean predicted 0.124 (prevalence z=+3.1). Low AUC with inflated prevalence points to label noise rather than prevalence shift. Its updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 4.4, mean cos -0.68, z around -9), and its O/E ratio is elevated in both sex groups and in income group 6 (about 7.0), consistent with flipped labels. Per-round CITL is negative from round 2 on, so the fault appears to start at round 1. Confidence is slightly lower because the per-round signal for VT is noisier.

report.summary: I screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income). Three clients stand out consistently across tools: CT, UT and VT. Each has an anomalous update profile (large norm ratios, strongly negative cosine to the median update), a low local AUC (0.57-0.62), strongly negative CITL, and observed prevalence well above what its predictions and features imply. That pattern fits flipped outcome labels (label_noise), not poisoning, since local performance is abnormal. Their O/E inflation is spread across subgroups rather than concentrated in one group, so subgroup_bias is ruled out, and drift shift_sd values are small, so drift is ruled out. Other weaker leads (GU's sex-group drift and small-sample update norm, CT's age-group-12 O/E, WV and IL feature outliers) were single-statistic deviations from small or noisy clients, with no second independent tool pointing the same way, so I did not report them. Budget was fully spent (20.0 epsilon) across the screens and confirmation calls.
